target.title: fix(mcp-apps): reject non-canonical CSP metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the MCP App sandbox HTTP origin accepted non-canonical variants of CSP metadata issued by OpenClaw. Appended junk, base64url padding, and extra JSON fields could all select the same sandbox policy as the canonical query value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sandbox decoder now requires both the base64url bytes and the normalized CSP envelope to round-trip exactly to OpenClaw's encoder output. CSP normalization, policy construction, size limits, and the sandbox route are unchanged. Risk is limited to rejecting aliases of OpenClaw-owned metadata; the production-function proof covers the canonical value and each rejected alias.

## User Impact

Malformed or structurally altered MCP App CSP query metadata now fails closed instead of being accepted as a valid sandbox policy. Canonical sandbox URLs produced by OpenClaw continue to decode normally.

## Evidence

On Node v24.18.0, I drove the real exported `buildMcpAppSandboxPath()` and `decodeMcpAppSandboxCsp()` production functions with the same harness against unmodified `upstream/main` and the fixed branch.

Before, the canonical value and all three non-canonical variants were accepted as the same policy:

```text
BEFORE canonical: accepted {"connectDomains":["https://api.example.com"]}
BEFORE appendedJunk: accepted {"connectDomains":["https://api.example.com"]}
BEFORE padding: accepted {"connectDomains":["https://api.example.com"]}
BEFORE extraField: accepted {"connectDomains":["https://api.example.com"]}
```

After the fix, the canonical value still decodes while the altered values fail closed:

```text
AFTER canonical: accepted {"connectDomains":["https://api.example.com"]}
AFTER appendedJunk: rejected MCP App CSP metadata is not canonical
AFTER padding: rejected MCP App CSP metadata is not canonical
AFTER extraField: rejected MCP App CSP metadata is not canonical
```

The focused decoder and HTTP-origin regressions pass, including assertions that the malformed query values return HTTP 400:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-sandbox-http.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       19 passed (19)
```

Also run: targeted `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, and Codex autoreview (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.94, no actionable findings). No browser-rendered MCP App was run; the affected behavior is the deterministic query decoder and HTTP rejection path before app content is served.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review the change; the production-function proof and focused tests were run manually.
